title: Burgess Shale
summary: Fossil deposit in Yoho National Park, British Columbia, with exceptionally preserved soft-bodied Cambrian animals. Charles Walcott found the fossils in 1909 and collected thousands of specimens. The Burgess Shale Formation is about 507 million years old and a standard reference for early animal life.

uncertainty.note: The ROM species pages give "around 507 million years old" for the Burgess Shale Formation (Wuliuan Stage); the Burgess Shale Geoscience Foundation says 508 million. The range covers both.

as_recorded.value: Middle Cambrian, Wuliuan stage, Burgess Shale Formation (around 507 million years old)

when.display: about 507 million years ago (Middle Cambrian, Wuliuan)

where.modern_name: Walcott Quarry, Fossil Ridge, Yoho National Park, British Columbia, Canada
where.historical_name: Deep-water marine basin on the western margin of Laurentia; no polities exist at this date

paleo.note: MERDITH2021 returned no reconstruction (999.99) for this point at 500-510 Ma, so the PALEOMAP value is stored. It is indicative only.

importance.justification: The classic Cambrian soft-bodied fossil site, whose 1909 discovery shaped views of early animal life.

reviewer_note: Age differs between sources (ROM about 507 Ma; foundation 508 Ma). Coordinates are the Wikidata point for the formation (51.4333 N, 116.467 W), near the Walcott Quarry; UNESCO's Canadian Rockies listing gives only a park-wide point so it was not used. The ROM introduction page was used for location in Yoho National Park. MERDITH2021 failed for this point, hence the PALEOMAP fallback.
